title: Treasury coupon announcement (10-Year TIPS new issue + 20-Year bond reopening + 6/13/26/52-week bills) — the MLK-shifted January block, whose TIPS number is published 71 days early
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), re-fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-09 by this event's own initial research (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes), text layer decompressed stream-by-stream and re-tokenised into 909 tokens. SIX securities carry announce date `Thursday, January 14, 2027`, read verbatim and INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED against the proposal that created this event: `6-Week  BILL`, `13-Week  BILL`, `26-Week  BILL` and `52-Week  BILL` (all auction Tuesday, January 19, 2027, settle Thursday, January 21, 2027), `20-Year  BOND` + `R` (auction Wednesday, January 20, 2027, settle Friday, January 22, 2027) and `10-Year  TIPS` + `T` with NO `R` (auction Thursday, January 21, 2027, settle Friday, January 29, 2027). The PDF's own legend, also read verbatim, is `T --denotes TIPS` and `R --denotes reopening`, so the 20-Year leg is a reopening and the 10-Year TIPS leg is a NEW ISSUE. The PDF carries its own line `Holiday - Monday, January 18, 2027 - Birthday of Martin Luther King, Jr.`, which is why all four bills auction Tuesday rather than the usual Monday/Tuesday split. The ~11:00 a.m. ET announcement slot is standing convention inherited from the sibling coupon-announcement ledgers and is NOT separately sourced. Stays estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the confirming primary is the announcement itself. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN by this event's own initial research (2026-09-09), which read the single prior proposal (`proposals/treasury-coupon-announcement-2027-01-14.from-treasury-10y-tips-2027-01-21.json`, 2026-09-09) in full first, per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md. THE FINDING THAT INVERTS THE PROPOSAL'S FRAME, and the reason the title changed: the proposal called this 'where the 2027 TIPS size actually prints' and 'the session it becomes public, seven days before the auction'. It is not. Treasury's quarterly refunding statement names every TIPS auction of its own quarter BY NAME AND BY NUMBER, including new issues, and the November refunding covers the November-to-January quarter. Read verbatim from sb0305 (the 2025-11-05 refunding statement, fetched direct this session, HTTP 200, 90,570 bytes): 'Over the November 2025 to January 2026 quarter, Treasury plans to ... maintain the January 10-year TIPS new issue auction size at $21 billion.' The 2026-01-22 auction then printed exactly $21B. So this event's headline number becomes public at the 2026-11-04 refunding, 71 days before the announcement reads it back, and 2026-11-04 — already tracked as `treasury-refunding-2026-11-04` — is this event's real decision date. THE STRUCTURAL TWIN, EXACT AND ALREADY SCORED: the 2026-01-15 announcement (fiscaldata `announcemt_date`, pulled 2026-09-09) carried the identical six securities — 13-Week $89B, 26-Week $77B, 52-Week $50B, 6-Week $85B (all auction Tue 2026-01-20), 19-Year 10-Month 20-Year reopening $13B (auction Wed 2026-01-21) and the 10-Year TIPS new issue 91282CPU9 $21B (auction Thu 2026-01-22) — MLK-shifted the same way (MLK 2026-01-19). Both coupon legs printed exactly what sb0305 had named 71 days earlier; the only numbers that moved were bills, 13-week +$3B and 6-week +$10B, and sb0305 had pre-announced even that in writing: 'by the middle of January 2026, Treasury anticipates increasing bill auction sizes based on expected fiscal outflows.' TWO BASE-RATE CORRECTIONS this session makes to claims this calendar's sibling ledgers rely on, both from pulling the TIPS record back to 1997 (fiscaldata auctions_query, `inflation_index_security: Yes`, 268 rows across two pulls) rather than to 2018 or 2023. FIRST: the proposal's counter-case — 'the 10-Year series has never held one size for four consecutive new issues ... each of the three prior runs that reached three was ended by a step-up at the fourth, 3 of 3' — is a window artifact. The full continuous semiannual record (46 new issues, January/July without a gap since 2004-01) contains a run of NINE ($15B, 2012-01 through 2016-01) and a run of SIX ($13B, 2016-07 through 2019-01). Of six prior runs that reached three, only TWO broke at the fourth; four held. SECOND, and it fires the 2026-11-12 sibling's own headline leg: that ledger's central finding is that 'a TIPS size change has never expressed at a reopening.' It has. CUSIP 912828N71 (new issue 2016-01-21, $15B) was reopened at $11B on 2016-03-17 and again on 2016-05-19 — a $4B gap where the -$2B rule says $13B, the only two off-rule reopenings in 64 in the whole record — and the NEW ISSUE followed four months later, cut to $13B on 2016-07-21. The reopening led the new issue, which is exactly the sequence the sibling's leg says cannot happen; the claim is true inside a 2023+ window and false on the record. THE HONEST OPEN NUMBER IS THE BILLS, AND JANUARY IS WHERE THEY MOVE: benchmark-bill size changes since 2023 cluster in January — 13-week 75->77 and 77->79 plus 26-week 68->70 in January 2024, and 13-week 86->89 plus 6-week 75->85->90 in January 2026 — so 2 of 3 recent Januaries carried an increase, both on the third-week auctions this announcement sizes. The 52-week (the only monthly bill here, $52B since 2026-07-07) changed in 1 of 3 Januaries. SOURCED HOLIDAY ARTIFACT for whoever researches the 2027-01-19 bill auctions: a 52-week bill displaced to Tuesday by a Monday federal holiday closes at 1:00 PM ET, not the standard 11:30 AM — 11 of 11 such displacements since 2022 (fiscaldata `closing_time_comp`, n=100 since 2019), including 2026-01-20 and 2025-01-21, both MLK. THE 20-YEAR LEG IS THE SECOND REOPENING of the November 2026 new issue, on the Feb/May/Aug/Nov new-issue rotation: $13B for 24 consecutive reopenings since 2023-09-19, zero deviations, and $13B in each of the three observed January second-reopenings (2024-01-17, 2025-01-22, 2026-01-21). ONE dated adjacent event PROPOSED in the same PR: `treasury-20y-bond-2027-01-20`, the reopening auction this announcement sizes. The 10-Year TIPS auction 2027-01-21 is already tracked and is this event's proposer. The four bill legs are deliberately not filed: this calendar tracks no bill auction of any tenor, and inventing the class inside an adjacency sweep would be a scope decision, not a discovery.
